title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 54 (Issue of Sweat Equity Shares)

content.overview: Section 54(1) provides that, notwithstanding anything contained in section 53, a company may issue sweat equity shares of a class of shares already issued if: (a) the issue is authorised by a special resolution passed by the company; (b) the resolution specifies the number of shares, the current market price, consideration, if any, and the class or classes of directors or employees to whom such equity shares are to be issued; and (d) where the equity shares of the company are listed on a recognised stock exchange, the sweat equity shares are issued in accordance with the regulations made by the Securities and Exchange Board in this behalf, and if they are not so listed, the sweat equity shares are issued in accordance with such rules as may be prescribed. Clause (c) of sub-section (1) (one-year waiting period after commencement of business) was omitted by the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2017 with effect from 7 May 2018. Section 54(2) provides that the rights, limitations, restrictions and provisions as are for the time being applicable to equity shares shall be applicable to the sweat equity shares issued under this section and the holders of such shares shall rank pari passu with other equity shareholders. The expression “sweat equity shares” is defined in section 2(88) as equity shares issued by a company to its directors or employees at a discount or for consideration other than cash for providing know-how or making available rights in the nature of intellectual property rights or value additions, by whatever name called.
content.glance: Notwithstanding s. 53: special resolution specifying number, market price, consideration and class of directors/employees; listed → SEBI regulations, unlisted → prescribed rules; clause (c) one-year rule omitted; holders rank pari passu with other equity shareholders; definition in s. 2(88).
content.study: Notwithstanding anything contained in section 53, a company may issue sweat equity shares of a class of shares already issued, if the following conditions are fulfilled, namely: (a) the issue is authorised by a special resolution passed by the company; (b) the resolution specifies the number of shares, the current market price, consideration, if any, and the class or classes of directors or employees to whom such equity shares are to be issued; (d) where the equity shares of the company are listed on a recognised stock exchange, the sweat equity shares are issued in accordance with the regulations made by the Securities and Exchange Board in this behalf and if they are not so listed, the sweat equity shares are issued in accordance with such rules as may be prescribed (s. 54(1)). Clause (c) (not less than one year elapsed since the company commenced business) was omitted with effect from 7 May 2018. The rights, limitations, restrictions and provisions applicable to equity shares apply to sweat equity shares under this section and the holders rank pari passu with other equity shareholders (s. 54(2)). Under section 2(88), sweat equity shares means equity shares issued to directors or employees at a discount or for consideration other than cash for providing know-how or making available rights in the nature of intellectual property rights or value additions. Current-law framing: confirm special resolution and content of the resolution; apply listed/unlisted regulatory path; do not apply the omitted one-year condition; treat as exception to s. 53; note pari passu ranking and the s. 2(88) definition.

sections.heading: Exception to discount prohibition (s. 54(1))
sections.body: Notwithstanding section 53, a company may issue sweat equity shares of a class of shares already issued if the statutory conditions are fulfilled.

sections.heading: Special resolution (s. 54(1)(a)–(b))
sections.body: The issue must be authorised by a special resolution. The resolution must specify the number of shares, the current market price, consideration if any, and the class or classes of directors or employees to whom the shares are to be issued.

sections.heading: Listed and unlisted paths (s. 54(1)(d))
sections.body: If the company’s equity shares are listed on a recognised stock exchange, issue in accordance with SEBI regulations; if not listed, in accordance with such rules as may be prescribed.

sections.heading: Omitted one-year condition
sections.body: Former clause (c) (not less than one year since commencement of business) was omitted by the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2017 with effect from 7 May 2018 and is no longer a condition.

sections.heading: Rights and ranking (s. 54(2))
sections.body: Rights, limitations, restrictions and provisions applicable to equity shares apply to sweat equity shares; holders rank pari passu with other equity shareholders.

sections.heading: Definition (s. 2(88))
sections.body: Sweat equity shares means equity shares issued to directors or employees at a discount or for consideration other than cash for providing know-how or making available rights in the nature of intellectual property rights or value additions, by whatever name called.

examples.title: Compliant sweat equity
examples.body: After a special resolution specifying number, market price, consideration and class of recipients, and compliance with SEBI regulations (listed) or prescribed rules (unlisted), a company issues sweat equity to an employee for IP contributed. Section 54 is complied with; s. 53 does not void the issue.

examples.title: Missing special resolution
examples.body: Sweat equity is issued without a special resolution. Section 54(1)(a) is not satisfied.

examples.title: One-year rule no longer applies
examples.body: A newly incorporated company proposes sweat equity within months of incorporation. The former one-year condition in clause (c) was omitted from 7 May 2018 and is not a barrier under current law.

hypotheticals.question: Is sweat equity free of all capital rules?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. It is a regulated exception to s. 53 and must satisfy special resolution, resolution content, and listed/unlisted regulatory conditions under s. 54.

hypotheticals.question: Does the one-year waiting period still apply?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Clause (c) of s. 54(1) was omitted with effect from 7 May 2018.

distinctions.title: Sweat equity (s. 54) vs discount prohibition (s. 53)
distinctions.left: Regulated exception for directors/employees for know-how/IP/value additions
distinctions.right: General ban on issue of shares at a discount (with limited other exceptions)

misconceptions.trap: Any discounted issue to employees is automatically valid as sweat equity.
misconceptions.correction: Sweat equity requires a special resolution with specified particulars and compliance with SEBI regulations or prescribed rules, and a qualifying purpose under s. 2(88).

misconceptions.trap: Sweat equity cannot be issued until one year after the company commenced business.
misconceptions.correction: That condition (former clause (c)) was omitted with effect from 7 May 2018.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 54 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify proposed sweat equity (s. 2(88) definition). II. Check special resolution and content (number, market price, consideration, class of recipients). III. Apply listed (SEBI) or unlisted (prescribed rules) path. IV. Confirm clause (c) is omitted. V. Confirm exception to s. 53 and pari passu ranking. VI. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Special resolution and its content; listed/unlisted status and regulatory compliance; purpose (know-how/IP/value additions); precise relief.

examTips: Special resolution must specify number, market price, consideration and class of recipients.
Exception to s. 53; holders rank pari passu.

Clause (c) (one-year rule) is omitted. Sweat equity is defined in section 2(88).

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Notwithstanding section 53, a company may issue sweat equity shares of a class already issued if authorised by special resolution specifying number, current market price, consideration if any, and class of directors or employees, and if listed in accordance with SEBI regulations or if unlisted in accordance with prescribed rules. The former one-year condition was omitted from 7 May 2018. Holders rank pari passu with other equity shareholders. Definition is in section 2(88).

Issue without special resolution — fails s. 54(1)(a).
Issue within months of incorporation — one-year rule no longer applies.

Special resolution must specify number, market price, consideration and recipients.
